paragraphs.text: The proposer offers a technical solution that partially complies with the requirements for power distribution and redundancy. The solution includes 800 VDC two-wire distribution to the racks, sized for 198 to 330 kW racks in each 20 MW deployment unit, with a growth path to 570 kW per rack position. The distribution system supports fast shutdown by shunt trip, current-limited DC fault current, and two protection zones, ensuring insulation monitoring on the facility side and residual current monitoring at the rack interface (cites: [1], [15]).

The prefabricated modular power pods are designed for concurrent maintenance and the block-plus-catcher arrangement, meeting the redundancy requirements. The pods are suitable for outdoor use with ambient temperatures ranging from -30 to 40 °C, with stated derating above 40 °C. The solution includes upgraded outdoor enclosures to meet the C5 corrosion class and 120 mph wind rating (cites: [2]).

The liquid cooling system supports the availability target of 99.9% with concurrently maintainable coolant distribution units (CDUs). The CDUs are modular, placed in mechanical galleries, and designed for facility water up to 45 °C on the primary side, serving a technical-grade secondary loop to GPU cold plates at a design flow of at least 1.5 LPM per kW. The system includes direct-to-chip cold plates for GPUs, sized to the rack design (cites: [3], [37], [38]).

The proposer confirms compliance with the interface requirements for the offered equipment. The solution meets the 800 VDC input band, the 125 A interlocked whip, the 54 VDC in-rack bus, and the telemetry and control interfaces as listed. The cooling system interfaces include facility water up to 45 °C on the CDU primary side and a technical-grade secondary loop at 1.5 LPM per kW or more (cites: [63], [64]).
